summary: toLocaleDateString is locale/Intl-sensitive and therefore requires a runtime/Intl-compatible formatting layer rather than direct DateTime.ToString substitution.

target.notes: Delegate to an ECMA-402/Intl-compatible runtime with explicit locale/time-zone data.

semantics.invalid_date: locale representation of Invalid Date per Intl/host semantics

caveats: Exact output varies by locale data and implementation; tests should assert semantics under a controlled Intl environment rather than hard-code unrelated host culture output.

tests.name: locale/options influence output
tests.expected_behavior: returns an en-US locale-sensitive string using UTC

tests.name: options getters are observable
tests.input: let n=0; const o={get timeZone(){n++; return "UTC";}}; new Date(0).toLocaleDateString("en-US",o); console.log(n>0);
tests.expected_behavior: prints true in Intl-enabled environments because options properties are read
